findings.problem: The same nested-machine delegation step is written out eight times in `δ` (matching, miss, delete, replace, append, remaining, deleteCount, appendCount). Each time the code does the following. If q is the nested machine's halt state, it takes `TM.allReadBack` into the next controller state. Otherwise it runs the nested δ, destructures the 6-tuple, and re-wraps only the state component. The proof of `δ_right_of_start` then repeats the same argument for each state: `dsimp only; split; exact TM.rightOfStart_allReadBack ..; exact (nested).δ_right_of_start q iHead wHeads oHead`. Each repetition spells out the six-component tuple by hand, and the structure repeats across the roughly 125 lines. Adding a phase means copying a 8–9 line δ block and a 5 line proof block and re-editing the nested machine, wrapper constructor and successor in three places, with no check that the halt test and the nested δ refer to the same machine. The same shape also occurs in EntryScan/Defs.lean, which shows there is no shared helper.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a generic combinator and one preservation lemma, e.g. in Combinators/Helpers.lean next to `allReadBack`:

```lean
/-- Run nested machine `M` from state `q`; at its halt state, take the
content-preserving hand-off to `next`. -/
def TM.delegate {σ : Type} {n : ℕ} (M : TM n) (wrap : M.Q → σ) (next : σ)
    (q : M.Q) (iHead : Γ) (wHeads : Fin n → Γ) (oHead : Γ) :
    σ × (Fin n → Γw) × Γw × Dir3 × (Fin n → Dir3) × Dir3 :=
  if q = M.qhalt then allReadBack next iHead wHeads oHead
  else
    let (q', w, o, i, wd, od) := M.δ q iHead wHeads oHead
    (wrap q', w, o, i, wd, od)

theorem TM.rightOfStart_delegate {σ : Type} {n : ℕ} (M : TM n) (wrap : M.Q → σ)
    (next : σ) (q : M.Q) (iHead : Γ) (wHeads : Fin n → Γ) (oHead : Γ) :
    let (_, _, _, inDir, workDirs, outDir) :=
      TM.delegate M wrap next q iHead wHeads oHead
    (iHead = Γ.start → inDir = Dir3.right) ∧
    (∀ i, wHeads i = Γ.start → workDirs i = Dir3.right) ∧
    (oHead = Γ.start → outDir = Dir3.right) := by
  unfold TM.delegate
  split
  · exact TM.rightOfStart_allReadBack iHead wHeads oHead
  · exact M.δ_right_of_start q iHead wHeads oHead
```

The proof is a sketch and may need a `dsimp only` or `simp only` before `split`. With it, each δ case becomes one line. For example:

`| .miss q => TM.delegate (entryMissCopyTM tapes.entry) .miss (.remaining (TM.binaryPredTM tapes.remaining).qstart) q iHead wHeads oHead`

`| .remaining q => TM.delegate (TM.binaryPredTM tapes.remaining) .remaining .test q iHead wHeads oHead`

The other six delegating cases take the same form, with `.delete`, `.replace`, `.append`, `.deleteCount`, `.appendCount` and their halt targets `.deleteCount (...)`, `.remaining (...)`, `.appendCount (...)`, `.done`. The matching `δ_right_of_start` branches for those cases become `| miss q => exact TM.rightOfStart_delegate _ _ _ q iHead wHeads oHead`, and so on, with no `dsimp only; split` boilerplate. The `.matching` state keeps its custom halt branch, so it only partly benefits: its non-halt part can use the helper by being split into a halt-branch `if` plus `delegate`. The `.test` and `.done` cases stay as they are.
findings.benefit: The nested-machine hand-off and its left-edge invariant are stated and proved once. Each controller phase then becomes one line naming the nested machine, the wrapper and the successor, instead of an 8–9 line tuple-destructuring block plus a separate proof block. This removes the risk of a copy-paste mismatch between a state's halt test, its nested δ and its proof. The helper would also serve the identical pattern in EntryScan/Defs.lean and other controller files, which reduces maintenance across the machine library.
